harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as the cluster's internal NTP source (chrony local reference clock, stratum 10, serving 10.100.93.0/24) and node2 as a chrony client pointed solely at node1 (no public NTP servers). Verified sync working, then restarted both nodes one at a time, confirming boot-id changes and post-reboot recovery of the internal time-sync relationship.
actions_performed: Inspected default time sync (systemd-timesyncd) on both nodes, confirmed chrony available via apt
Disabled systemd-timesyncd and installed chrony on node1 and node2
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on both nodes for name resolution
Replaced node1 chrony.conf pool servers with 'local stratum 10' + 'allow 10.100.93.0/24', making it an internal time source
Replaced node2 chrony.conf pool servers with 'server node1 iburst', restricting sync to node1 only
Restarted chrony on both nodes and verified node2 synchronized to node1 (chronyc sources/tracking, chronyc clients on node1)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony health baseline on both nodes
Restarted node1 via 'sudo reboot' (backgrounded so ack returned), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and restored local-reference chrony service
Restarted node2 via 'sudo reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and restored sync to node1 (chronyc burst + tracking showing '^* node1')

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal NTP source (no public servers)
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node1 shows 'local stratum 10' + 'allow 10.100.93.0/24' replacing Ubuntu pool servers; chronyc tracking shows Stratum 10 self-reference; chronyc clients/serverstats shows node1 actively serving NTP requests to node2

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public server
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node2 shows only 'server node1 iburst' (pool lines removed); chronyc sources/tracking after burst shows '^* node1' selected as current best source with Reference ID node1
Captured boot_id 63f96994-951b-4597-aac7-233c38c86ce0 and healthy chrony (active, stratum 10) prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent call timed out (node down); later call returned new boot_id 4061e0c2-6f43-4d85-989b-514ff1802452, proving restart occurred
chrony active again post-reboot, still configured as local stratum-10 reference clock with allow rule for the subnet, config persisted across reboot
Captured boot_id 96c08b66-5aa4-4e9a-b76f-04e2c6e34ced and healthy chrony (active, stratum 11, synced to node1) prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent call reset (node down); later call returned new boot_id ad8f7891-3aed-4c66-9c0e-3847ab9bef8d, proving restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered state and re-established sync to node1 post-restart
evidence.summary: chrony active again post-reboot; after burst poll, chronyc sources shows '^* node1' selected and tracking shows Reference ID node1, stratum 11, confirming internal-only sync relationship survived restart
